--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_spring()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Place the nodes with the Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_spring()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Place the nodes with the Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm. title: >- [Graph.layout_spring()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Place the nodes with the Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place the nodes with the Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5790-L5932){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_spring( k=None, iterations=50, threshold=0.0001, weighted=None, initial=None, fixed=None, scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Spring layout](../assets/graphs/layout-spring.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, the cube graph (eight nodes, each joined to three others) scattered at random. On the right, layout_spring(seed=1) treats edges as springs and nodes as repelling charges, and the cube settles into one square inside another." width="100%"} Nodes behave like charged particles joined by springs: every pair repels with force `k^2 / d` and every edge pulls its ends together with force `w * d^2 / k`, where `d` is their distance, `w` the edge weight and `k` the ideal edge length. Starting from random positions, each iteration moves every node along its net force by at most the current "temperature", which cools linearly from a tenth of the starting area to zero, so the layout settles. The run stops early once the mean move falls below `threshold=`. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. Spring layouts are the general-purpose default: clusters pull together, bridges stretch between them and symmetric graphs tend to look symmetric. Each iteration costs `O(n^2)` (run in parallel on larger graphs), so use them up to a few thousand nodes. This ports NetworkX's dense `spring_layout()` scheme (NetworkX switches to a different energy-minimization method from 500 nodes; this method always uses the force iteration). Edge direction is ignored and parallel edges add their weights. The same `seed=` always gives the same layout, though not the same one as NetworkX, whose random numbers differ. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Ideal distance between adjacent nodes. If `None` (default), uses `1/sqrt(n)` (or the starting domain size over `sqrt(n)` when `fixed=` is given), which suits the unit square the layout starts in. Larger values spread the nodes apart. [iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[50]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations. Default is `50`. [threshold]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0001]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop once the root-mean-square move per node falls below this. Default is `1e-4`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use edge weights (`1` where missing) as spring strengths, so heavier edges pull harder. If `False`, every edge counts `1`. If `None` (default), follows whether the graph was created as weighted. [initial]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Union[str, dict]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Starting positions, as the name of a node attribute holding `(x, y)` pairs or a dict mapping node IDs or labels to pairs. Nodes without one start at random in a square as large as the given positions. If `None` (default), all nodes start at random in the unit square. [fixed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node IDs or labels that keep their `initial=` positions. When given, the result is not rescaled, so the fixed nodes stay where they are. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. `None` keeps the raw coordinates (`center=` is then ignored). Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random starting positions. If `None` (default), the layout differs on every call. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k=` is not positive, `threshold=` is negative, a `fixed=` node has no `initial=` position, an initial position is not a pair of finite numbers, `weighted=True` and an edge weight is negative, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The two communities of the karate club pull apart: ::: {#c59fd3a3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ( ec.karate_club() .layout_spring(seed=1) .plot(layout="pos", color_by="faction") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Positions from one layout can seed another. Here a spring layout refines a circular one while node `1` stays put: ::: {#6efb5854 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_lollipop_graph(6, 4).layout_circular(attr_name="start") pos = graph.layout_spring(initial="start", fixed=[1], seed=2, return_dict=True) pos[1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1.0, -1.2246467991473533e-17) ``` ::: :::
